# Sigma support and coverage

<!-- Generated by `python -m purplebench docs`; do not edit. `python -m purplebench docs --check` fails when it is stale. -->

This file is computed from the bundled rules in `backend/rules/` and the demo runs in `backend/data/demo_fixture.json`. The rules that PurpleBench's own evaluator supports are described in [SIGMA_SUPPORT.md](SIGMA_SUPPORT.md). Rules from SigmaHQ are under the [Detection Rule License 1.1](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/Detection-Rule-License); every rule below is shown with its author.

**What the numbers mean.** Coverage here is "this rule set on this recorded telemetry". A technique is `missed` when no rule in the set fired on it. It says nothing about any product, and nothing was executed.

## Bundled rules

| Rule set | Rules | Evaluated by PurpleBench | Unsupported |
|---|---|---|---|
| sigmahq | 58 | 54 | 4 |
| custom | 12 | 12 | 0 |
| **all** | **70** | **66** | **4** |

Rules outside the supported subset are reported as `unsupported` with the reason; they are never evaluated as "no match".

`untested` means the technique has no usable recorded telemetry in this data set. `[related]` and `[parent]` mark credit for a rule tagged with a related technique or the parent technique, which gives `partial`, not `detected`. Noisy rules (rules that also fire on the benign baseline) earn no credit and are named only when nothing else fired.
